name: docs-drift-gate-validates-claudemd-paths-and-managed-assets
title: Extend the CLAUDE.md docs-drift gate to validate path and managed-asset claims, not just command names
description: Today the docs-drift preflight gate (packages/main/src/handlers/validate-docs-drift.ts, consumed by review-preflight.ts / phase-gates.ts at REVIEW->TEST) DOES scan CLAUDE.md, but ONLY for lattice command-name references vs the registry. It does NOT validate path references or managed-asset claims. That is exactly the blind spot that let CLAUDE.md line 77 falsely state 'do not create .Codex/hooks' while the framework actually GENERATES those host hooks (the P3 contradiction). Meanwhile core/audit-scan.ts already implements scanPathDrift (and scanFlagDrift), but only the audit flow (handlers/audit.ts) uses it — it is not wired into the CLAUDE.md docs-drift gate. Outcome: extend the CLAUDE.md docs-drift gate so the main doc cannot drift/lie about (1) file paths it references that do not exist, and (2) managed assets — a 'do not create <X>' / 'X must not exist' claim for an <X> that the managed-asset registry (core/managed-assets.ts) says the framework generates must be flagged as drift. Reuse the existing scanPathDrift / managed-asset registry rather than re-implementing. Keep the existing command-name scan intact and additive (no behavior change for docs with no path/asset issues). Scope: validate-docs-drift.ts gate logic + reuse of audit-scan/managed-assets + a regression smoke wired into the validate battery. Out of scope: the actual one-line CLAUDE.md:77 wording fix (separate story B-94ae), the .Codex rename (B-ed70), and changing any hook generation behavior.
